mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has risen steadily for three consecutive weeks (from -3.9 to -1.1), indicating a gradual return of commuting and work-adjacent errands that feed retail and recreation footfall, so RETAIL_REC should trend higher over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved monotonically from t-3w to t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean is not higher than its last-28-day mean despite WORKPLACES continuing to rise, in over half of observed instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp week-on-week deterioration in TRANSIT mobility signals reduced willingness or ability to travel to commercial districts, which mechanically depresses RETAIL_REC within the following week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 1.0 point week-on-week after a prior improving streak
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT worsened from -12.4 at t-1w to -13.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises or stays flat in the week following a TRANSIT decline exceeding the trigger threshold.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility remains elevated while WORKPLACES mobility is simultaneously suppressed, households are substituting home-based routines for both work and errands, jointly compressing discretionary retail trips below what either series alone would predict.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above +5 while WORKPLACES remains below -2
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL at 6.4 and WORKPLACES at -1.1 in t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next two weeks despite RESIDENTIAL staying elevated and WORKPLACES staying suppressed jointly.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has stabilized near -9 for three weeks, indicating essential-trip demand has plateaued at a seasonal baseline; without further essential-trip growth, discretionary RETAIL_REC mobility will also plateau rather than grow over the next month.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM values cluster between -8.6 and -9.0 over the last three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean rises meaningfully above its last-28-day mean even though GROCERY_PHARM remains flat.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC improved for two weeks (t-3w to t-1w) then reversed sharply at t-0w; this single-week reversal is noise around an improving trend and will mean-revert upward within one week as behavior realigns with the underlying trajectory.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC drops more than 2 points in the most recent week after two prior weeks of improvement
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC moved -9.7 to -11.9 between t-1w and t-0w after improving the prior two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to decline or fails to recover toward the t-1w level within the next week.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous improvement in both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES over the prior three weeks reflects resumption of commuting infrastructure usage, which jointly amplifies weekday retail visits beyond what either series predicts alone, raising RETAIL_REC over the next month.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improve for two consecutive weeks simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES improved from t-3w to t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next four weeks despite sustained joint improvement in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility below a threshold signals relaxation of stay-at-home policy pressure, which frees discretionary movement and lifts RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below +5.5 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 7.0 to 6.0 between t-3w and t-1w before ticking up to 6.4
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next two weeks even after RESIDENTIAL falls below the threshold for two consecutive weeks.
